CH states that at +0x2cc the target advances both pointers IN PLACE while ours materialises a fresh register off a surviving base, and prescribes attacking `dst2 = dst + d8` as that base. Quoting r3's definition site as the run-37 dispatch rule requires: r3 at +0x2d0 is defined at +0x2bc by `mulli r3,r0,6`, so r3 is the shared `adv` TEMPORARY, not a pointer. The target's two pointer advances are `add r9,r9,r3` at +0x2d8 and `add r10,r10,r3` at +0x2e8, both reading that one temporary, exactly as ours do; and the target forms dst2 at +0x2b0 as `add r10,r9,r5` = dst + d8, the very derivation CH proposed to remove. So +0x2cc is a two-word schedule-and-register difference on a shared temporary, NOT a base asymmetry, and dst2's dependence on dst is the TARGET'S OWN shape. Consistent with that, MWCC re-CSEs the independent spelling back to `add r10,r6,r9` in the else branch, and a split probe confirmed the whole 119 -> 117 gain came from the count>0x100 branch alone while the else branch's spelling is score-invariant. hypothesis.statement: The remaining 95 words are ~8 in the case-2 init block and ~87 of pure volatile-bank renaming in the two y-loops, and the volatile cascade is anchored on TWO callee-saved webs ours fails to place: the target puts the inner counter `x` in r21 and `dst2` in r19 (both reused dead-parameter registers, param_5 and param_4), while ours puts `x` in r19, spills `dst2` to the volatile r12, and spends r21 as a short-lived scratch. Within-block declaration reordering of {dst,dst2,x} is MEASURED DEAD (two orderings, both neutral at 95/184) - do not re-probe it. The untried lever is a LIVENESS change rather than a naming change: HOIST dst, dst2 and x out of the per-iteration `for (y...)` block into the enclosing `if (count > 0x100)` block's declaration list (and likewise in the else branch), so their live ranges span the whole y-loop instead of restarting each iteration. A longer live range is what earns a callee-saved register, and it is the one thing within-block reordering cannot change. This is NOT contradicted by the byte-identical function-scope hoist recorded here: that probe moved locals that ALREADY held callee-saved registers, so it changed naming only, whereas these two hold none.
